addendum_hash_recipe.note: Recompute from this committed file alone; depends on every field except addendum_hash.

amendment_rule: Any change to the canonical selection or the SUI ceiling must be published as a dated successor artifact stating what changed and why, alongside the version it replaces. A silent edit invalidates the pre-registration property of the SUI stream.

canonical_batch_rule.multi_batch: only freeze ts with freeze->publish latency within the ceiling qualify; the LATEST qualifying freeze ts wins (most information, least staleness)
canonical_batch_rule.none_qualify: an anomaly the published rule does not cover: raise, never guess. Silently grading an unqualified batch is exactly the failure the rule exists to prevent.
canonical_batch_rule.per_day: sole batch -> kept unconditionally; the rule only arbitrates between batches of the SAME UTC day

contributes_zero_anchors: This artifact cites nothing and CAN anchor nothing. It carries no rows key; its artifact field contains 'addendum', so _is_non_anchor_artifact excludes it by TYPE even though prereg/sui/ is in PREREG_ANCHOR_DIRS (the whitelist the SUI stream joined when the resolution path was enabled).

day_later_manifest.note: The full-open-set re-publication created 2026-08-14T00:44:01Z carries 66 rows and re-carries both 08-13 batches. Re-publication cannot move a batch's first publication: only the EARLIEST created_utc wins, so A and B keep the latencies above.

disclosure.duplicate_batch_day: 2026-08-13 produced TWO frozen SUI batches: ts 1786654800 (2026-08-13T21:00:00+00:00) and ts 1786662000 (2026-08-13T23:00:00+00:00). Both carry the same 22-pool reserve cohort — the same pool set, the same rows. This is the same defect class as the duplicate 2026-07-30 SOL batches disclosed in prereg/solana/20260803_112507_solana_addendum_20260730.json.

freeze_to_publish_latency.note: Computed as first_publication_by_freeze_ts(ts) - ts, i.e. the earliest created_utc of any committed manifest carrying that freeze ts, minus the freeze ts. Identical to the latency a third party computes from the publiciq repo alone. Note the SUI stream republishes the complete open set, so several manifests carry both freeze ts; only the EARLIEST created_utc wins.

disclosure.the_rule: The canonical-batch rule from prereg/solana/20260803_112507_solana_addendum_20260730.json (commit bb699cb) applies, with the SUI ceiling: per UTC day, a sole batch is kept unconditionally; multiple batches -> only freeze ts whose freeze->publish latency is within the ceiling qualify; the LATEST qualifying freeze ts wins; a day where none qualifies is an anomaly and raises rather than guesses. Applied via canonical_freeze_ts(..., max_latency=SUI_CEILING_SEC) — the same code the resolution path (resolved_sui) runs.

governs: The 44 rows of the two duplicate 2026-08-13 SUI freeze batches (2 x 22 pools): ts 1786654800 (2026-08-13T21:00:00+00:00) and ts 1786662000 (2026-08-13T23:00:00+00:00), first published in prereg/sui/20260813_214412_sui_preregistered_at_prediction.json and prereg/sui/20260814_001409_sui_preregistered_at_prediction.json respectively. This artifact pre-commits that ts 1786662000 is the canonical batch the 2026-08-27+ resolution will be allowed to grade, and that ts 1786654800 is published-but-non-canonical. Rows first frozen on ANY other date, and the resolution outcomes themselves (which land in the hash-signed grade ledger, never here), are not covered by it.
outcomes_known_at_issue: ZERO. No SUI prediction has resolved. The 2026-08-13 23:00:00Z cohort matures 2026-08-27T23:00:00+00:00. Every number in this artifact was derived at build time from the committed SUI manifests and the published canonical-batch rule; none was chosen with knowledge of an outcome, because no outcome exists to know.

su_max_publish_latency_ceiling.why: A tier-3 ('preregistered_at_prediction') claim asserts publication AT prediction time, on the same UTC day. SOL's ceiling is 900s (TIER3_MAX_PUBLISH_LATENCY_SEC), calibrated to the SOL 12:20Z pipeline that freezes, emits, commits and pushes in one invocation. The SUI freeze runs on its own cadence and its pre-registration lands up to ~2h after the freeze instant (observed 2026-08-13: 2652s and 4449s). Applying the SOL 900s ceiling to SUI would make EVERY SUI day an unqualified anomaly. 7200s is the pre-committed middle: wide enough to absorb the SUI operational reality and never tripped by normal variance, still a real same-day claim, and nowhere near a half-day hold. It is tunable via SUI_TIER3_MAX_PUBLISH_LATENCY_SEC, never hardcoded to a timestamp.
su_max_publish_latency_ceiling.wired_as: prereg_emit_recorded.resolved_sui() calls canonical_freeze_ts with max_latency=SUI_TIER3_MAX_PUBLISH_LATENCY_SEC (env-overridable default 7200), so a reader can verify this ceiling is what the resolution actually applies.
